Naomi / team — quick nodepool recommendations for ACME pilot: 

- Cluster layout (high level):
  - Control plane: 3 dedicated control-plane nodes (CPU-only), small VMs/servers (16 vCPU, 64GB RAM), tolerations to prevent eviction. Keep them separate from workload pools for stability.
  - Infra pool: 2-3 medium CPU nodes (32 vCPU, 128GB) for logging, monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana), and Rook/Ceph daemons where applicable.
  - Workload pools (inference):
    - GPU pool: use dedicate nodes with A100 cards. For pilot (targeting up to 6 concurrent hosts), recommend starting with 3 GPU nodes configured with 2 x A100-80GB per node (or the closest physical config). Example: 3 x (2xA100, 512GB RAM, NVMe local SSD) to provide headroom for batch and streaming workloads.
    - CPU pool: for auxiliary inference & low-cost fallbacks, 4-6 CPU nodes (48–96GB RAM) sized to host model loaders and light inference traffic.

- Autoscaling:
  - On-prem, prefer Cluster-Autoscaler with a custom provisioner tied to your provisioning tool (e.g., MAAS, MetalLB + IPAM) or use a metal-focused autoscaler like OpenKruise/Karpenter with a custom webhook if you have dynamic bare-metal provisioning. For this pilot, recommend static node pools + scheduled scaling (cron) to limit complexity; enable cluster-autoscaler only once CI/CD/provisioning is vetted.

- GPU runtime and drivers:
  - Preinstall NVIDIA drivers, nvidia-container-toolkit, and the NVIDIA device plugin. Match driver/CUDA combos to the CUDA version the model runtime expects. Document driver version matrix in runbook.
  - If nodes support MIG, carve profiles for smaller workloads; otherwise prefer using whole-GPU allocation to simplify runtime scheduling.

- Runtime considerations:
  - Use node labels (e.g., node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true, redwood/role=inference) and PodTopologySpread to distribute load across racks for fault tolerance.
  - Set kubelet eviction thresholds and pod disruption budgets for model-serving pods (minAvailable=1 per model shard).
  - Use a DaemonSet for kube-proxy and any node-local cache agents; consider a node-local NVMe cache to shrink model pull times.

- Networking: short notes (I'll leave deeper details to Marissa): ensure MTU consistency, implement Calico for NetworkPolicy enforcement, use MetalLB for load balancing, and place inference egress behind a controlled NAT for auditability.

Attached is a quick sizing spreadsheet I used in other on-prem pilots. I also included suggested taints/tolerations and example K8s resource requests/limits.

Adding storage + networking ops guidance for ACME: 

Storage recommendations:
- Topology: given ACME already runs Ceph, recommend Rook-managed Ceph for block PVs (RBD) and object (RGW) if they want S3-compatible model stores. Rook simplifies lifecycle and ties well into K8s.
- Storage classes: create two primary classes — fast-ssd (replicated RBD on NVMe) for model caches and hot workloads; standard-hdd (replicated) for logs and archives.
- PV sizing: model cache PVs should be node-local or use a ReadWriteOnce PVC on SSD-backed RBD. Typical model image sizes: 10–80GB depending on model; reserve 2x model size for cache + temp. For a pilot with 6 replicas, plan 1TB fast-ssd reserve.
- Snapshots & retention: use Ceph snapshots for point-in-time; schedule daily snapshots and keep a rolling 30-day retention for hot data. Move older snapshots to object store if required.
- Encryption & KMS: use dm-crypt/LUKS at the OSD level and integrate Vault for key management. If customer uses an external HSM/KMS, configure Ceph to use their KMS provider.
- CSI and driver ops: use Rook-Ceph CSI; ensure you pin CSI driver versions to avoid unintended upgrades. Test snapshot and clone flows during validation.
- Node-local cache: for inference latency, use node-local caches (e.g., cache warmer sidecar + local NVMe) to avoid r/w hot spots on Ceph for repeated model loads.

Networking ops notes:
- CNI: Calico (v3+) for NetworkPolicy and BGP support if they want pod-to-pod routing across racks. Ensure IPIP/BGP is configured for the leaf/spine setup.
- Service mesh: not required for initial pilot; keep simple. If using mTLS later, plan for cert rotation (cert-manager + Vault).
- Load balancing: MetalLB in BGP mode is a stable option for bare metal LB. Use nodePort only for internal test routes.
- Egress & audit: central egress NAT + proxy so we can capture and audit outbound calls; flow logs should be sent to a central syslog/ELK.

Observability & compliance:
- Logging: Fluentd/FluentBit to push to central ELK/Graylog. Ensure structured logs for inference requests for later QOS analysis.
- Tracing: lightweight tracing (OpenTelemetry) to capture request path and tail-latency.
- Audit logs: enable Kubernetes audit-policy, ship to centralized storage with 1-year retention.

Operational checklist for pilot:
1) Confirm hardware mapping (which servers have GPUs).
2) Prestage images and driver versions; verify driver/CUDA compatibility.
3) Deploy Rook-Ceph to the infra pool with 3 OSD nodes (min for replication).
4) Deploy control-plane and infra pools, then schedule the GPU pool.
5) Validate model pull + node-local cache performance.
6) Run failure scenarios (rack failure, OSD loss) and verify recovery time objectives.

Hi Susan — thanks for the details.

Summary of recommended pilot plan (ops-level):
- Cluster layout: 3 control-plane nodes (CPU-only), 2–3 infra nodes for monitoring/rook daemons, 3 GPU nodes for inference (target 2xA100 per node where available) and 4 CPU worker nodes for fallback.
- Storage: use Rook-managed Ceph (RBD + RGW) with two storage classes (fast-ssd for hot model caches, standard-hdd for logs). Recommend node-local NVMe caches for model pulls and daily snapshots with 30-day hot retention.
- Autoscaling: start with static node pools and scheduled scaling for the pilot; enable cluster-autoscaler after provisioning automation is validated.
- Networking & LB: Calico for NetworkPolicy, MetalLB (BGP) for load balancing, central egress NAT for auditability; ensure MTU consistency across leaf/spine.
- Security: encrypt at rest via Ceph KMS integration (Vault/HSM) and enable k8s audit logs with 1-year retention shipped to central logging.
- Ops & observability: Prometheus + Grafana for metrics, FluentBit for logs, OpenTelemetry for tracing. Validate during pilot: model load latency, tail latency under concurrency, and recovery from node/rack failure.

1) We propose a 2-week on-site workshop to map hardware to node pools and stage drivers/images (tentative window: late July).
2) Please complete the attached questionnaire so we can prepare exact resource maps (attached: onprem-k8s-questionnaire.pdf).
